A machine learning approach is presented that accelerates DFTB simulations by predicting optimal initial atomic charges and demonstrates that ML-predicted initial charges consistently and significantly improve SCC convergence across diverse chemical systems including organic molecules, biomolecules, water clusters, transition metal oxides and solid electrolytes.

Vilya-1 is introduced, a deep learning model that addresses two central challenges in macrocycle design: sampling biologically relevant conformations across arbitrary chemistries and predicting key developability properties such as membrane permeability.

This workflow demonstrates the feasibility of integrating a SERS-active membrane with a machine learning workflow to streamline sampling, detection, and automated data interpretation, marking an important advancement toward the development of field-deployable SERS-based platforms for easy and user-friendly nanoplastic monitoring.

The results establish the framework as a reliable tool for studying multi-disorder alloys, with applications to complex disordered systems such as high-entropy alloys, multiferroics, and spintronic devices.

This work demonstrates that integrating cell-free enzyme engineering with machine learning enables opportunities for high-throughput experimental measurements to benchmark and improve protein language models, accelerate design loops, and expand functional exploration within protein families where experimental information is limited.

GenLoop with dtSFM brings directed evolution to small molecules through computational-thermodynamic selection through computational-thermodynamic selection; wet-lab validation is the immediate next step.

A pipeline that runs end-to-end from a corpus of 11,083 recent condensed-matter physics arXiv papers to a publication-grade manuscript with three substantive physics findings is presented, laying a foundation for autonomous research in high-stakes scientific domains beyond computational physics.

The identified compounds, STOCK4S-00019 and STOCK4S-00025 (hit2), show strong potential as CDK2 inhibitors and support their further investigation through experimental validation and highlight the effectiveness of integrated computational approaches in anticancer drug discovery.

A computational prioritization framework for identifying TNF-α inhibitor candidates and mechanistic insights into their binding behavior is provided and the identified compounds warrant further experimental validation for their therapeutic potential in LDH.

A graph-based multivariable framework for brain imaging analysis that integrates key organizational principles of brain function-including segregation, integration, modularity, and temporal dynamics-within a unified graph neural network architecture is proposed.

Ariadne, a decoder-only route generator that represents the target, optional constraints, and route in one prompt-completion sequence, is introduced, a decoder-only route generator that represents the target, optional constraints, and route in one prompt-completion sequence.

OakuloidTM, an open DILI prediction framework that pairs a leakage audited structure based model with an optional iBAC 3D primary human hepatocyte IC50/Cmax confirmation signal, is presented, supporting reproducible DILI screening and benchmark auditing.

NaDC and DCA demonstrate anti-influenza activity both in vitro and in vivo, reducing viral replication and alleviating inflammatory lung injury and position NaDC and DCA as promising lead compounds for anti-influenza drug development and provide a foundation for further mechanistic validation.

This work trains neural networks on quantum data generated from approximate ground states of the two-dimensional Heisenberg XXZ model and shows that they can accurately predict spatially resolved observables for previously unseen Hamiltonian parameters, both within the training distribution and in an out-of-distribution regime approaching the phase boundary.

A biologically enriched heterogeneous knowledge graph (KG) integrating clustered mutations, synthetic lethal interactions, drug structures, protein sequences, and functional annotations is constructed, designed to enable the identification of actionable diagnostic signatures and precision therapeutic strategies by leveraging multi-layered biological network factors.

A class of sequence kernels that exploit evolutionary substitution matrices as well as local linearity are introduced and it is demonstrated that the resulting Gaussian processes provide data-efficient models of protein property landscapes, frequently outperforming alternatives that rely on foundation model embeddings.

A Gaussian-process (GP) surrogate model for the normal-incidence reflectance spectrum of one-dimensional GaAs/Al distributed Bragg reflectors (DBRs) establishes a rapid surrogate for DBR design-space exploration.

An evaluation shows that model-generated SMILES embeddings can expand the applicability domain, indicating a more robust representation of structural information compared to traditional molecular descriptors in traditional QSAR approach.

A proteomics-based DRN model (Pro-DRN) is developed and substantially enhanced early risk stratification beyond conventional clinical factors and may support targeted screening and timely neuroprotective interventions, advancing molecularly guided strategies for diabetic eye disease prevention.

ESM3-PPISites enables accurate interfaces identification without relying on complex structural inputs at inference time, establishing a reliable and computationally efficient strategy for mapping protein-protein interaction sites.

The potential of Synthesa AI to enhance pharmacological evidence synthesis by improving the reproducibility and comprehensiveness of systematic reviews used to evaluate drug efficacy, safety, and therapeutic positioning is highlighted.

This work presents a machine-learning accelerated atomistic modeling approach for the phase stability of (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3 perovskites (where FA is formamidinium), that explicitly accounts for finite-temperature entropy effects.

PRISM (Position-encoded Regressive Inverse Spectral Model), a unified decoder-only autoregressive transformer that streamlines this process by jointly predicting discrete material selection and continuous thickness regression within a single backbone, offering a highly efficient alternative to classical optimization methods.

DeepMetabio-mCRC Screener demonstrated that ACMSD predicts CRLM risk, postoperative recurrence, metastatic mechanisms, and therapeutic responsiveness to EGFR/VEGFR-targeted agents, supporting its application in personalized treatment strategies.

Netsene provides a structurally robust, bulk platform that unifies ultrahigh carrier mobility, topological nodal surfaces, and potential correlation physics, demonstrating the power of theory-guided, machine-learning-accelerated discovery for engineering topological quantum phases.

RCI is introduced, a novel ML-supported SCI framework that reframes determinant selection as a pairwise ranking problem and provides a lightweight and modular plugin that can be seamlessly incorporated into other supervised learning frameworks.

Results demonstrate that GAN-based data augmentation can effectively mitigate data sparsity and class imbalance in spectral classification of common plastics, providing a practical foundation for creating robust online polymer classification systems.

AlignReact is introduced, a novel chemical reaction representation learning framework that explicitly integrates atomic correspondence between reactants and products into the network architecture, enabling the model to perceive and model molecular structural transformations during reactions.

MT-ConBiFormer-GPT is introduced, a deep generative model designed explicitly for low-data, multi-target molecular generation, focusing on the critical PI3K–AKT–mTOR cancer signaling pathway, and presents a flexible and computationally efficient framework for multi-target drug discovery in data-limited settings.

The nonlinear relationship between the governing physical parameters and the resulting flow and heat transfer behaviour is modelled using an artificial intelligence-based neural network framework that has been optimized using the Intelligent Bayesian Regularization technique.

To the knowledge, these are the first computationally proposed de novo miniprotein candidates designed to occlude the IL-23R-binding face of IL-23 p19 and a length-robust interface metric derived from AlphaFold-initial-guess predicted aligned error is used.

A novel prediction model that leverages representation learning to capture the complex features of protein-DNA interfaces, providing a reliable model for mapping the energetic landscapes of protein-DNA interfaces and verified via permutation tests that PDI-Spot captures biologically meaningful patterns beyond random chance.

Overall the MACE models are shown to most accurately reproduce the potential energy surface, with little sign of overfitting, but at a significant computational cost, highlighting important questions regarding the choice of models in computational materials science.

A cross-scale transfer-cascade learning framework that transforms the structural–activity patterns of molecular antibiotics into predictive principles for the surface ligands of nanoparticle antibiotics, and identifies a new class of 24 surface ligands with high predicted antibacterial efficacy for decorating gold nanoparticles across over 9 million molecules.

This Review systematically evaluates the structural trade-offs in MLIP design: the undersampling of highly strained configurations, the prohibitive computational overhead of high-order message-passing architectures, and the necessity of nonlocal interactions for open and field-coupled systems, and establishes a framework for observable-specific validation.

MARCO establishes a Dual-Layer defense that simultaneously protects intellectual property and ensures the forensic traceability of potential biosecurity misuses, and achieves superior fidelity and robustness while successfully validating watermark transferability.

This work proposes SoftGene, a novel framework for LLM-based gene set annotation that leverages the hierarchical structure of gene sets and constructs a hybrid prompting scheme that combines soft prompts derived from gene set embeddings with hard prompts containing auxiliary context generated by an LLM.

A framework for learning ab initio phase-field models, where the mesoscopic equation is not postulated but derived from a Mori-Zwanzig projection of molecular dynamics onto species-density fields under explicit assumptions, to provide a mesoscopic counterpart to ab initio molecular dynamics.
A comprehensive, first-principles-derived database of two-atom interaction potentials and interatomic forces to accelerate the property prediction via physics-informed machine learning is presented.

HADRec is proposed, a Hierarchy-Aware Drug Recommendation framework that integrates molecular knowledge with electronic health records (EHRs) and establishes HADRec as a high-performance, interpretable, and clinically grounded pathway toward safe and reliable AI-driven medication recommendation.

A potential is presented that is universal within the class of water-free solid-state hydrogen-bond network mediated proton conductors rather than across chemistry and a database of 4.4 million first-principles configurations spanning 55 materials, offering a template for other compound classes.

This work couples coordinated variation with thermodynamic selection, offering a novel paradigm for RNA design that achieves leading performance on multiple benchmarks, and reveals thermodynamic gains, policy dynamics, and robustness across settings.

Atelier is a self-supervised framework that amortizes INR fitting for reconstructed cryoEM maps, a transformer-based hypernetwork that generates high-fidelity reconstructions across a wide range of protein structures, including large multi-subunit assemblies.

SpecOpt is introduced, a molecular design task that seeks constrained structural modifications to an existing compound that increase its binding preference for an intended target over known off-targets while preserving its structural identity and drug-like properties.

It is suggested that MIR-derived information could contribute to a biologically meaningful, scalable composite physiological profiling framework at the individual cow level, although further validation with independent clinical or physiological reference data is required.

This study establishes an exploratory screening workflow for hypothesis generation and prioritization based on observational associations and introduces a Task-Adaptive Representation Approach to alleviate the over-encoding of historical prescription information within diagnostic vectors, enabling the robust prioritization of generated hypotheses.

A sequence-based framework that integrates RNA tertiary structural modeling, local geometric feature extraction, and machine learning to predict capsid protein binding sites is presented, providing new mechanistic insights into RNA–capsid interactions and establishing a foundation for extending this approach to diverse ssRNA viruses.

This approach provides an interpretable AI strategy for uncovering the communication mechanisms that underlie folding, allostery, and long-range signal propagation in molecular machines, while also supporting AI-guided modulation of biomolecular function and rational protein engineering.
Squidly surpasses state-of-the-art ML annotation methods in catalytic residue prediction while remaining sufficiently fast to enable wide-scale screening of databases.

RBMD 2.0, a major new release of the random batch molecular dynamics package designed for cross-node multi-GPU simulations of large-scale systems, combines the improved random batch Ewald method with three-dimensional domain decomposition and ghost-particle communication to accelerate multi-GPU nonbonded force evaluation.

Comprehensive evaluations across multiple biomolecular NMR experiments demonstrate that CLEAR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art reconstruction methods, reducing reconstruction errors (RLNE) by approximately 16-25% while exhibiting overall superior or competitive performance across multiple quantitative metrics, including weak-peak preservation, under severe nonuniform sampling conditions.
MAPViS provides a scalable multimodal framework for joint activity-toxicity modeling and offers a practical computational tool for antibiotic virtual screening and candidate prioritization.

This study explores the properties of multiwalled WS2 nanotubes using the CHGNet universal machine-learning interatomic potential (uMLIP) and the atomistic force field previously developed by the team, revealing excellent agreement in structural features between the approaches.

An interface for hybrid machine learning/molecular mechanics (ML/MM) simulations implemented in the widely used MD code GROMACS is presented, providing a practical foundation for incorporating machine learning potentials into production MD simulations of biomolecular systems.

UBio-MolFM lifts that ceiling: a foundation model trained on 160 million quantum-chemical labels, its receptive field spanning non-covalent distances at near-linear cost, and first-principles simulation is in reach.

TransTS is designed to provide reliable TS initial guesses for subsequent quantum-chemical refinement, where generated structures are evaluated not only by geometric similarity but also by their ability to converge to validated saddle points and recover the intended reaction pathways after refinement.

This work introduces a scalable TDA framework for extracting information on PPIs directly from localized protein surface patches that leverages multiscale topological descriptors, evaluated from patch-wise point cloud representations of protein mesh surfaces, combined with supervised machine learning models for interface prediction.

This work proposes a machine-learning charge density route for predicting defect formation energies with higher data efficiency and shows that charge-density learning enables more robust cross-size transfer than direct energy-force fitting and that mixed-size data design can substantially reduce the cost of defect prediction.

This work presents a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approach to identify advanced dynamic magnetic-field-temperature paths that create skyrmions with enhanced thermal stability and suggests that a physics-informed DRL framework streamlines the identification of optimized protocols for skyrmion creation.

ASE2SPRKKR is presented, a comprehensive Python interface that integrates SPR-KKR into the Atomic Simulation Environment (ASE), making SPR-KKR more accessible, streamlined, and uniform and establishes a replicable blueprint for bringing other specialized Green's function and first-principles codes into the collaborative, reproducible workflows that modern materials discovery requires.

This scoping review investigates the current state of PK property prediction of small molecules in drug discovery using machine learning methods and a combination of machine learning and mechanistic models and proposes leveraging the pattern recognition capabilities of deep learning models in conjunction with the biological interpretability provided by mechanistic approaches.

An uncertainty-guided surrogate framework that predicts, directly from geometry, the three fields governing erosion: per-triangle normal impact velocity, tangential impact velocity, and particle impact flux is presented.

The EC-Reason-Bench is proposed, a training-free, diagnostic evaluation protocol built to answer two questions: why general LLMs score close to nothing on EC number prediction, and how much of that loss can be recovered without updating a single weight.

Transformer Atomic Cluster Expansion (TRACE) is introduced, an energy-conserving architecture that combines atomic cluster expansion density correlations with local multihead cross-attention that captures multi-species crystallization, liquid structures, phase diagrams, and chemical reactivity.

A benchmarking framework is introduced to evaluate both the equilibrium and far-from-equilibrium performance of state-of-the-art uMLIPs, including two MACE-based models, two PET-based models, MatterSim, and a custom MACE model trained exclusively on elemental data.

Structural investigation of re-docked actives showed that re-ranked poses were more native-like, with improved binding-site occupancy, reduced centroid displacement, and greater recovery of co-crystal interactions.

This work introduces a methodology for performing anharmonic vibrational structure calculations that can be deployed in a hybrid, quantum-classical mode and demonstrates a hybrid, quantum-classical computational workflow in which a quantum sampling algorithm provides the seed.

The development of LogPpred, an AI-based predictor of molecular lipophilicity, a robust, accurate, and transparent tool for the early assessment of molecular lipophilicity in medicinal chemistry and drug discovery is reported.

Compared to conventional expectations, it is found that simpler models with interpretable features can achieve competitive performance under rigorous validation protocols and should become a requirement for future ML studies for reaction-yield prediction.

GEM-GPT is introduced, a transcriptomics-guided framework that generates personalized therapeutic candidate molecules intended to shift cell type-specific disease states toward healthy phenotypes and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, produces cell type-resolved molecules, and generalizes to unseen cellular contexts.

A substrate-specific allosteric ligand-design strategy that integrates all-atom molecular dynamics simulations, conformational clustering, machine-learning-based ligand generation, and surface-wide docking-based selectivity screening is established, using collagen-bound MMP1 as a model system.

The proposed NIRS‐ML ensemble model offers a scalable, non‐destructive solution for real‐time RM monitoring, supporting pharmaceutical manufacturing within the PAT framework and its adaptability across formulations highlights its potential as a versatile tool for lyophilized biopharmaceutical manufacturing pipelines.

The Transferable Water Implicit Network (TWIN) is introduced, an implicit water MLP parametrized entirely by an Equivariant Graph Neural Network and trained solely on ab initio and experimental labels, consistently outperforming previous machine-learning-based implicit solvent or coarse-grained models.

SoluBench, a benchmark comprising 9806 questions across four tasks of increasing complexity, designed to evaluate LLMs' performance on solubility tasks in both pure and mixed solvent systems, demonstrates that while LLMs possess intrinsic chemical analysis capabilities sufficient for qualitative solubility assessment in technological practice, significant limitations in molecular structure understanding persist.

The results demonstrate the feasibility of NIRS combined with machine learning for preliminary origin traceability of D. crepidatum and provide spectral clues for future investigation of origin-related chemical variation and quality discrimination.

The Bayes-optimal RMSD (BRMSD) is introduced, which optimizes per-atom weights jointly with structural averages by maximizing a Bayesian posterior and controls the transition from classical RMSD to a progressive focus on a rigid core.

PEPstrMOD2 provides a powerful, high-throughput, and highly accurate platform to facilitate peptide-based drug development and structural biology research, and removes peptide length restrictions through AlphaFold2 and ESMFold integration.

This study proposes a novel computational method for multiproperty optimization in the molecular structure design of bioactive molecules using multicontext (i.e., chemically and genetically perturbed) transcriptome data on human cells and demonstrates that the proposed method consistently yields molecules with more favorable drug-like characteristics than existing methods.

This review traces the history of MPI research, from curated resources and early cheminformatics to harmonized identifiers, proteome-scale structural models, and artificial intelligence–driven prediction, while highlighting persistent challenges that continue to limit mechanistic interpretation of metabolites.

CoTAR is presented, a hybrid graph neural network (GNN)–hidden Markov model (HMM) framework that reconstructs bond connectivity and order, formal charges, and unpaired electrons from atomic species and coordinates by combining learned local environments, chemical constraints, and temporal smoothing.

This review provides a comprehensive and critical synthesis of AI-assisted SERS platforms for cardiovascular diagnostics, integrating advances in plasmonic materials, biomolecular recognition, and intelligent spectral analysis within a unified framework.

This work proposes a dual-channel fusion uncertainty-aware network (DFUN) for automated space group classification and incorporates Monte Carlo Dropout to provide predictive uncertainty estimation, thereby enabling not only accurate classification but also a crucial assessment of the model's reliability.

A physics‐informed machine learning framework for unified‐composition Q&P steel design, enabling multiple strength grades from a single alloy via heat‐treatment tuning and exemplifies a paradigm for sustainable alloy design that reduces chemistry variants while simplifying recycling.

TC-SOH is introduced: a modular, plug-and-play service architecture for autonomous, end-to-end SOH prediction that outperforms the considered physics-informed and data-driven baselines, reducing MAPE by 1.91 times and RMSE by 2.13 times.

A two-stage automated framework is proposed that identifies the minimal global reaction network via sparse optimization and then generates and discriminates interpretable rate expressions using symbolic regression (SR) with model-based design of experiments, opening a pathway to accelerate knowledge discovery and build physics-grounded digital twins for reaction engineering applications.

This work combines diffusion models from the field of materials science with techniques originally developed in computer vision for image inpainting to enable a much faster and more accurate completion of host structures, compared to unconditioned diffusion models or previous approaches solely based on density-functional theory (DFT).

It is found that foundation model quality, correct E0 initialisation, and well-chosen hyperparameters are prerequisites whose impact routinely exceeds that of the fine-tuning strategy itself, and most strategies achieve strong target-task accuracy, consistently surpassing models trained from scratch.

The results demonstrate that shared physics-guided degradation priors enable robust generalization across previously unseen battery chemistries, including LFP systems, while substantially reducing the need for chemistry-specific laboratory characterization and calibration procedures.

A benchmarking of 15 pretrained MLIPs provides an objective basis for practitioners to select the most appropriate MLIP for their own simulations and offers insight into which factors most strongly influence model accuracy.

SECS is a framework that combines contrastive learning with evolutionary algorithms to automate structure elucidation directly from raw, multimodal spectroscopic data and demonstrates how synergistic combination of machine learning paradigms can solve analytical bottlenecks that have constrained chemical discovery.

The information bonus (IB), a task-level metric that measures the linearly accessible advantage of frozen single-sequence AlphaFold2 Evoformer representations over frozen ESM-2 embeddings under protein-level cross-validation, is introduced and turns representation selection into a measurable decision for AI-for-science systems.

AMix-2 is presented, a protein-text foundation model that establishes protein as a native modality in large language models (LLMs), unifying protein understanding and sequence design within a single foundation model that outperforms frontier LLMs and demonstrates competitive performance to task-specific protein models.

Cognitive Loop via In-Situ Optimization (CLIO), an agent that couples a continuously-updated belief-state graph with a recursive plan-then-act loop, is presented, an agent that has the capacity to recognize when its own tools or assumptions are failing, to adapt its strategy in response, and to generate mechanistic hypotheses that guide experimental revision.
Extensive experiments on four battery domains show that BatteryMFormer consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, marking a significant step toward reliable BDTF.

DeepDOX1 is presented, a dual-drive DPA prediction tool featuring the tight integration of a concise AI architecture and an interpretable, quantum chemistry-based representation of protein–ligand interactions that outperforms popular AI-based DPA prediction methods in the tests simulating real-world hit-to-lead optimization (HLO) scenarios and a highly challenging test set featuring covalent ligands.

A multistage computation pipeline is demonstrated successfully on a puzzle comparable in complexity to Eternity II and with a known solution, based on multiple hybrid optimization steps with both “hard” and “soft” constraint formulations, identification of persistent substructures, and a final classical refinement stage.

In effort to standardize the evaluation of LLM agents on small molecule design, SMDD-Bench is introduced, a challenging, multi-turn, long-horizon agentic benchmark consisting of 502 guaranteed-solvable task instances spanning 5 task types: 2D Pharmacophore Identification, Interaction Point Discovery, Scaffold Hopping, Lead Optimization, and Fragment Assembly.
Oral multi-drug resistome sequences can be predicted using the GAT model, which can also be applied to future resistant sequences.

This work generalizes the reinforcement learning contracted quantum eigensolver (RL-CQE) to electronic excited states and real-time quantum dynamics, in which a deep Q-network agent adaptively selects the two-body operators at each iteration, yielding more compact ansätze and improved robustness with respect to critical hyperparameters.

An algorithm for evaluating contracted Clebsch--Gordan tensor products in $\mathcal{O}(L^3)$-equivariant machine learning potentials at fixed Canonical Polyadic (CP) rank is presented and extended to parity-aware equivariant message passing in atomic-cluster-expansion-style architectures.

This work enhances the previously proposed, symmetry-agnostic, All-atom Diffusion Transformer (ADiT) by introducing SymADiT, a symmetry-aware variant, and uses a representation of crystals based on Wyckoff positions to perform generative modelling in latent space.

Experiments show that specialized models excel at signal-level modeling, while MLLMs exhibit strengths in high-level reasoning but lack precise spectral grounding, and highlights the need for spectrum-native foundation models.

Experimental results demonstrate that MP2D consistently outperforms existing multi-objective baselines, achieving robust and balanced improvements across all objectives without retraining generative models, and highlight MP2D as a practical and scalable solution for multi-objective functional protein design.

Virtual screening of the DrugBank library identified six candidates, three of which, Carbimazole, Crizotinib, and GSK2018682 reduced TGF-β–induced collagen production and glycine accumulation in human lung fibroblasts, demonstrating transfer learning as a strategy for repurposable drug identification in data-scarce metabolic targets.

This paper introduces two acquisition signals derived directly from a pretrained MACE potential: a finite-width neural tangent kernel (NTK) and an activation kernel built from hidden latent space features that consistently outperform fixed-descriptor baselines, committee disagreement, and random acquisition.
A reproducible ligand-based approach for supporting the early-stage identification of potential MERS-CoV Mpro inhibitors using molecular representations derived from SMILES strings is presented.

This study demonstrates the feasibility of LLM-assisted structure-property prediction and virtual screening for NIR-II fluorophores, providing an efficient computational strategy for candidate prioritization and molecular optimization.

A knowledge graph-assisted machine learning model: Uncertainty-Calibrated Evidence-Chains (UCEC) for prioritizing NP-disease associations and generating traceable mechanistic hypotheses for subsequent validation is proposed.

DC-FLOW is proposed, a staged generative framework built around Delayed-Coupling Flow Matching that improves cyclization fidelity, diversity, and interface energetics, substantially increasing the yield of confident cyclic peptide binders under a fixed final-candidate budget.
Iso-EPIGS makes accurate isotope-effect simulations feasible for complex systems and lays the groundwork for foundation models of isotope effects across chemical space.

This work establishes a scalable paradigm for high-throughput chirality discrimination with particular promise for pharmaceutical enantiomer screening using machine learning on left- and right-circularly polarized dark-field RGB images, eliminating the need for spectral acquisition.

An optimized version of this criterion for out-of-distribution performance with structure disjoint splits, allowing for computationally feasible application on the public libraries, finds that at this scale the graph percolates.

NEMORA, a neural equivariant extension of the Fast Multipole Method, is introduced, a neural equivariant extension of the FMM for learning long-range tensorial representations that evaluates in linear time and memory complexity, allowing it to treat larger systems than other long-range methods reaching hundreds of thousands of atoms.

A lightweight, tool-augmented framework in which a locally deployable compact language model plans calls to 18 modular tools, while a Unified Molecular Schema maintains shared molecular records, while a plug-in interface supports tool replacement and extension is presented.

A machine‐learning‐driven peptide evolution platform is used, the Protein Optimization Engineering Tool (POET), to design and optimize short Gd‐binding motifs that enhance longitudinal relaxivity (r1) and demonstrate a generalizable framework that integrates computational evolution with biophysical screening to discover new biologically derived Gd‐binding motifs.

It is demonstrated that droplet deposition imaging combined with artificial intelligence provides a promising, rapid, and non-destructive strategy for pharmaceutical concentration analysis and quality assessment.

SALA is introduced, a flow-matching model built on state--context separation that evolves only asymmetric-unit atomic coordinates and symmetry-compatible lattice parameters while predicting their updates from the full periodic environment, and enables end-to-end generation of complex, symmetry-constrained molecular crystals.

A versatile multiscale framework is introduced that directly connects molecular-level electrostatics to collective properties via a colloid-inspired coarse-grained modeling combined with neural network-assisted optimization to decode charge-driven interactions in complex biomolecules and, more generally, in heterogeneously charged soft-matter systems.
This study introduces an advanced computational paradigm for therapeutic design targeting TM domains and provides a promising strategy to combat multidrug-resistant Gram-negative pathogens.

This study introduces a coupled simulation workflow that combines classical molecular dynamics with high-throughput quantum mechanical analysis to reveal the electronic structure signatures of mutation-induced drug resistance in the HIV-1 protease, and argues that this type of analysis may pave the way for designing inhibitors that maintain binding stability against systemic, mutation-induced destabilization.

A hybrid quantum neural network framework is introduced designed to extract quantitative parameters, such as phase weight fractions and scale factors, directly from one-dimensional powder diffraction patterns without iterative refinement, paving the way for using quantum computing hardware to analyse real-world materials characterisation data.

Computational strategies ranging from machine learning-guided sequence optimization to structure prediction and generative AI have accelerated the rational design of aptamers tailored to GBM specific challenges, enabling the development of innovative aptamer drug conjugates for targeted delivery to GBM cells.

It is found that random forest machine-learning models constructed using suitable structural features were able to distinguish oncogenic and benign mutations effectively and identified and utilized some features associated with these motifs for classifying EGFR mutants.

A coordination-informed machine-learning workflow reconstructs metal–ligand graphs from design-stage ligands for logβ1 prediction by exploiting privileged 3D/quantum-chemical pretraining of phenanthroline-derived ligands for predicted logβ1 prediction.

Geometry-optimized structures generated using the Universal Models for Atoms MLIP, trained on the Open Molecular Crystals 2025 dataset, were used to verify selected structures from the Cambridge Structural Database with the aim of detecting issues in both the interpretation of the original X-ray experiments and the performance of the used MLIP.

AutomaticXRD is proposed, an autonomous large language model (LLM) agent framework that organizes powder-XRD analysis as stepwise refinement, grounds actions in observed evidence, and applies deterministic crystallographic and physical checks before accepting results.

A structure-based computational pipeline was used to identify and evaluate inhibitors targeting the NDST1 sulfotransferase domain, and four chemically distinct small-molecule scaffolds and three peptide candidates were identified as stable binders to the NDST1 active site.

This multi-modal, cross-species framework demonstrates that integrating structural encodings with ADME descriptors enhances both predictive performance and interpretability, yielding hypothesis-generating attributions for structural optimization that warrant prospective experimental validation.

Current evidence suggests that no single material system simultaneously optimises UV-blocking efficiency, ROS control, biocompatibility, and industrial scalability, highlighting the need for multifunctional hybrid design strategies.

Attention analysis reveals that the proposed novel method for predicting reaction conditions in organic synthesis effectively captures critical motifs closely related to synthetic reaction conditions and exhibits interpretable capabilities.

AIMe (AI Molecule Explorer), a multi-agent neuro-symbolic AI framework that transforms the interpretation of unknown spectra into an omics-scale exploration across the known structural space, providing chemically interpretable annotations, is introduced.

This approach enables the direct prediction of the ELF and optical constants from measured REELS spectra with reduced computational cost as compared to the previous RMC method, and the predicted ELFs from ML exhibit high accuracy as verified by sum rules.
An interpretable, honestly benchmarked multi-objective pipeline that optimizes known anti-S.

A semiempirical extended tight-binding approach (GFN1-xTB) is employed to compute the electronic properties of a dataset of MOFs, and it is shown that GFN1-xTB approximates MOF band gaps well, as compared to semilocal DFT.

An advanced identification platform that integrates single-cell Raman spectroscopy with a self-attention mechanism (SAM)-driven convolutional neural network (CNN) configuration, which can realize convenient, non-destructive, high-precision identification of microsporidian spores from 11 various host sources at a single-cell resolution level is proposed.

The authors develop a machine learning classifier through the integration of 25,000 proteomics experiments to construct a wiring diagram of human cells, which enables structural modeling of disease-relevant complexes and establishes a highly accurate protein wiring diagram of the cell.

A comprehensive evaluation of CHIMIYA-1, a proprietary autoselection foundation model developed by Covenant Biosciences, against the full TDC ADMET Group, showing particular strength on toxicity and physicochemical-property endpoints.

This work combined ab initio optical-property calculations with a tabular foundation-model regression to predict the real and imaginary components of the frequency-dependent dielectric function for Mo-W-S-Se-Te TMD alloys, and predicted derived optical quantities, including refractive index, extinction coefficient, and absorption coefficient.

This work introduces a multi-modal deep learning architecture that jointly processes multiple signal representations, including raw time-series data, wavelet-based images, and static feature vectors, and demonstrates the potential of machine learning to enable robust, high-accuracy molecular identification with nanopore sensors.

LatticeMind is introduced, a validation-gated agentic framework that converts natural-language requests into executable, checkable density functional theory (DFT) projects and establishes workflow contracts, deterministic validation, bounded repair, and traceable records as a practical foundation for reliable AI-assisted scientific computing.
Classical sensitivity analysis and duality thus offer a rigorous, label-free audit that complements existing evaluation of AI-generated optimization models.

Assessment of pose prediction methods when the bound structure of a reference ligand is known and the likely binding mode(s) of a related compound are needed, and this work focuses on cases where the new compound has multiple potential binding modes.

A review of recent progress in AI-assisted biosensor development highlights how AI can link molecular design, device engineering, and signal interpretation to accelerate the development of next-generation biosensors.

AI2Pot is presented, a scalable and unified MLIP framework that seamlessly integrates model training, evaluation, and large-scale MD simulations with PyTorch-compatible ecosystem, and offers an user-friendly end-to-end framework for the developing, training, and deploying MLIPs for large scale MD.

A workflow for its feasibility is established by combining first-principles calculations and machine learning to quickly predict SHS reactions of MAX and MAB phases, confirming the practical utility of the calculated thermodynamic properties and  T  ad  .

This work compares role specifications in which the language model acts as equation author, candidate decider or search controller, alongside end-to-end language-model and purely numerical baselines and suggests that language models should shape hypothesis exploration rather than decide which equations survive.

This review contextualizes the historical trajectory of peptide-based vaccinology, from early linear epitope discoveries in the 1960s to sophisticated multi-epitope constructs and clinically tested candidates like UB-612 and PepGNP-Covid19, and examines critical challenges in immunoinformatics, including performance gaps in epitope prediction tools, complexities in human leucocyte antigen (HLA) mapping, and the need for extensive manual intervention in pipelines.

PFFIN is introduced, a data-driven framework for discovering protein units by jointly learning structural partitioning and functional supervision that partitions each protein into multiresidue units, with functional supervision that shapes the partition.

BOBa is introduced, a bandit-guided surrogate optimization framework that eliminates full-library inference by adaptively allocating computation across partitions of the action space and reveals a tunable tradeoff between screening performance and surrogate inference cost.

It is found that GNNs exhibit high seed-dependent variability in connection with the comparatively small training sets common for bioactivity measurements, highlighting the necessity of multiseed evaluation for robust model assessment.

Nanobody–antigen molecular recognition underpins nanobody discovery and development, necessitating accurate determination of binding occurrence, interface residues, and affinity, and this work presents NanoBind, a mechanism-driven deep learning framework that embeds the CDR-dominated binding pattern within its encoder, enabling robust prediction of binding occurrence and interface residues from limited NAI data.

It is discovered that early layers rely on position-tracking latents to parse molecular grammar, while later layers encode atom-in-substructure and pharmacologically relevant features, and it is shown that non-canonical SMILES produce more disruptive representation shifts than invalid SMILES, driven by position-latent disruption propagating across layers.

The proposed RL–DRO framework achieves a superior trade-off between cost efficiency and operational robustness when compared with deterministic, stochastic, and standalone reinforcement learning benchmarks, and unifies data-driven adaptability with theoretical robustness.

The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated by predicting the compositional dependence of various materials properties—including stacking-fault energies, short-range order, heat capacities, and phase diagrams—for the AuPt and CuAu binary alloys, the ternary CrCoNi, and the TiTaVW high-entropy alloy.

The feasibility of label-free, machine learning–assisted Raman profiling to resolve clinically relevant glioma subtypes at single-cell resolution is supported and this scalable analytical framework provides a translational platform for investigating metabolic heterogeneity, therapeutic response, co-culture systems, and patient-derived organoid models.

This work provides a feasible computational paradigm for rapid discovery of high-energy, low-sensitivity energetic materials within a fixed scaffold using density functional theory and machine learning to address these issues.

A path forward is outlined that prioritizes community datasets compliant with Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, and Reuse (FAIR) principles, transparent evaluation suites, and interpretable, uncertainty-aware models capable of reliable deployment across laboratories and devices.

A target-driven virtual screening study using TAME-VS against aldo–keto reductase 1C3, an enzyme implicated in cancer progression and chemoresistance, demonstrating enhanced inhibitor prioritization and functional relevance by generalization to chemically different scaffolds and prospective evaluation under constrained synthesis capacity.

DeepRoot is a multi-agent LLM system that jointly builds and utilizes a verified knowledge graph, showing that grounding and reasoning -- often conflated -- are separable axes the system can compose for therapeutic reasoning.

This work proves equivariance, expressivity, and cohomological-correspondence results for the Equivariant Cellular Sheaf Networks, and validate them numerically: the Hamiltonian-to-sheaf embedding is exact to machine precision, the cohomology dimension reproduces non-bonding-orbital counts across eleven conjugated molecules.

This work studies one cell line and assay, THP-1 cells profiled by DRUG-seq, scored by the active-compound weighted MSE(wMSE) of the VCPI prediction contest, and proposes a staged approach combining a frozen chemistry embedding with retrieval-support features to predict the residual over the mean.

A deep learning framework is introduced that reconstructs a provable “digital twin” of the thermodynamics recorded in cryo-EM data, enabling precise thermodynamic analysis using only cryo-EM data and revealing insights into biomolecular dynamics without supplementary assumption.
This work demonstrates how reactivity-informed ML can extract physically meaningful trends from heterogeneous AAS data and guide source-dependent binder design.

A 511-sequence library is constructed and sequence charge decoration weighted by chain length, SCD × N, is found to be a compact, interpretable organizing coordinate for CALVADOS-2-derived IDP salt response and provide a polymer-physics, feature-level complement to ensemble-level generative models.

DeltaDiff is introduced, a physics-guided inference framework for mutant-structure generation that incorporates mutation-aware physical guidance into a baseline diffusion model that captures key mutation-induced conformational changes without requiring retraining or fine-tuning of the baseline model.
A tractable first step toward model-level exact inverse design of copolymers under the two-layered model is given by introducing a simple feature representation, called the mixing vector (MV) model.
OpenADMET facilitates an era of rational, multi-parameter drug design by creating pre-competitive, mechanistic datasets that build generalizable models grounded in structural “ground truth”.

A transferable and efficient framework for constructing high-accuracy potential energy surfaces for weakly bound molecular complexes by employing an uncertainty-driven active learning strategy and a constrained transfer learning approach.

A Dirichlet flow-matching model that initializes generation from lineage priors derived from ancestral sequence reconstruction, turning generation into structured mutation from an evolved scaffold is proposed.

Metadynamics Discrete Neural Sampler (MetaDNS), a general framework integrating well-tempered metadynamics into discrete diffusion or autoregressive samplers, achieves comparable exploration requiring fewer bias deposition steps.

This work establishes a new benchmark for food authentication using AI, offering a highly accurate, scalable and transparent solution with significant potential to be incorporated into a real-time and portable food safety systems to allow on-site verification.

Simulation schemes based on efficient machine learning representations of the potential energy surface (PES) predicted by ab initio calculations have become increasingly popular over the past decade, and reveal that formic and acetic acids control the wettability of TiO2 largely through acid–base chemistry at the interface rather than chemisorption on the oxide surface, a finding that could help improve the design of self-cleaning surfaces and photocatalytic devices.

This review discusses the most important TME biomarkers, such as tumor budding (TB), tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), and tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs), with emphasis on their prognostic and predictive significance.

This proposal proposes two networks trained jointly on independent bootstraps with a sym-KL consistency loss between their predictions, which at matched $2{\times}$-ERM compute reduces churn a further median $45\%$ beyond bagging-$K{=}2$.

This work reframe the search for alternative molecular conformations as that of sampling from a diffusion distribution conditioned using any arbitrary Bayesian likelihood, and implements a twisted diffusion sampler in Boltz-2 to sample this conditioned distribution.

Residual-Aware Deep-learning–Assisted Refinement for Powder Diffraction (RADAR-PD) is introduced, a modality-aware machine learning framework for phase identification and quantification across both x-ray and neutron powder diffraction.

The MeTime package builds upon a central S4 container that stores multiple datasets, associated metadata and analysis outputs, enabling unified handling of complex longitudinal studies, making MeTime a versatile platform for longitudinal omics workflows.

StrAcTable, an automatically constructed dataset of annotated protein-ligand complexes, is created, enabling an efficient construction of training and validation datasets for structure-based molecular design method development.

This work demonstrates that discrete diffusion fine-tuning achieves strong language modeling performance on antibody sequences while allowing for generation conditioned on any off-the-shelf classifier, and introduces germline absorbing diffusion, a novel modification of the discrete diffusion noise process in which the germline sequence serves as the absorbing state.
The Spectral Model eXplainer (SMX), a post-hoc, global, model-agnostic XAI framework that explains spectral classifiers through expert-informed spectral zones, is introduced.

It is demonstrated that lightweight, physics-based guidance can significantly enhance generative drug design while preserving chemical validity and diversity and provides a principled justification for its stabilizing effect.

Non-Uniform ViT is introduced, a simple, general-purpose vision transformer that redesigns image tokenization, data representation, and positional encoding to respect the structure of Fourier-space data.

This narrative review synthesizes advances in artificial intelligence applications in hepatitis research and clinical practice published over the past decade, organized across three clinical domains: diagnosis, treatment optimization, and prognosis prediction.

It is argued a pre-trained model may already contain useful molecular edits that zero-shot generation cannot efficiently reach, and proposed ReMedI, which uses the molecular language model as a base proposer for inference-time alignment, is proposed.

A synergy-aware flow matching framework that anchors the source distribution at an additive prior and learns a residual flow toward the true perturbed state, and incorporates perturbation-conditioned gene interaction modeling, which provides a biologically grounded and robust framework for single-cell perturbation response prediction.

How active learning has evolved from a niche, on-the-fly training technique for query-by-committee and Gaussian process force fields into a diverse family of data-efficient strategies into a diverse family of data-efficient strategies is surveyed.

A large-scale multimodal SP dataset of 13,546 standardized multiplex images from 5,477 patients across 35 cohorts and five major SP technologies is presented, along with a benchmark suite spanning cell phenotyping, diagnostic and therapeutic prediction as well as virtual staining tasks across twelve cohorts that places current SP foundation models on common ground against task specific baselines.

This Perspective argues that MLPs can be made more accurate than their training methods non-empirically by generalizing across a third space, that of quantum-chemical methods, and proposes routes to method-transferable MLPs that predict at unseen methods.

Together, these results show that current LLM agents can autonomously develop high-performing molecular prediction and optimization methods across substantially different drug-discovery settings, in several cases matching or exceeding leading human-developed approaches.
Neural Petri Flow is introduced, which learns this rate law, or a readout for classification, and hard-wires the rest as parameter-free layers on one firing vector.

A unified approach to classical force fields, which learns both bonded and nonbonded parameters simultaneously and simultaneously from ab initio reference data, and reproduces the conformational sampling of both classical and existing machine-learned FFs, without relying on externally assigned nonbonded parameters.

This work introduces Mosaic, a hybrid mesh-particle representation that partitions space into anchored regions containing atom slots, providing persistent spatial addresses for local conditioning, hierarchical generation, and scalable assembly of large, heterogeneous structures.

The results establish that diversity-aware search broadens the set of docking-predicted interaction hypotheses generated under a fixed budget; they do not experimentally establish distinct binding modes or biochemical activity.

GraPPI is established as a generalizable framework for protein-complex representation learning, extending pretrained protein representations from individual proteins toward the interaction context in which protein function is realized.

TRIDENT-2 is presented, a multimodal artificial intelligence model for predicting chemical toxicity across evolutionarily diverse eukaryotic species, demonstrating that artificial intelligence can help overcome longstanding data limitations in ecotoxicology.

This work proposes three testable criteria for assessing the foundational nature of molecular models, shifting the notion of a molecular foundation model from a descriptive label to a testable hypothesis, offering a framework for assessing current models and guiding future developments.

Spatial Clinical Explainability is presented, an explainable graph neural network that identifies tissue patterns predictive of clinical outcomes in spatial proteomics datasets that identifies spatial and protein-expression patterns associated with cancer progression and patient survival.

This work identifies the mathematical consequence of chaining together Dropout and LayerNorm and provides a free, principled adjustment to improve the evaluation performance of many pretrained models.

The FuTCM-PDD provides an AI-assisted framework for phenotype-based discovery of potential drug candidates from CMM through multi-level data fusion, helping move beyond the recurrent prioritization of commonly reported associations in conventional network pharmacology and supporting the identification of pharmacologically relevant candidate compounds associated with specific phenotypic contexts.

BC-GNN integrates sequence-informed auxiliary transition estimation, boundary-aware propagation, boundary-aware propagation, microenvironment-aware channel recalibration, and hierarchical multi-scale integration (HMSI) to improve structural representation learning and demonstrate that BC-GNN is effective for RNA-ligand binding-site prediction.

This work devised a Turing imitation game inspired experiment to compare two deep learning methods, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), for generating experimentally viable de novo antibody sequences, highlighting the promise of computationally driven discovery of antibody-based biotherapeutics.

Results show that an AI scientist workflow can propose thermal structures, test them under common constraints, and quantify their electrical cost, and show that lower temperature can accompany higher thermal resistance when current falls.

This systematic review aims at outlining the recent efforts for creating noninvasive alternative procedures via machine learning (ML) in deprived regions and a less resource‐demanding alternative would be beneficial.

Equivariant-Free Transformer-Autoencoded Latent Flow Matching is introduced, a two-stage framework that samples a fixed-dimensional latent vector using flow matching and employs an autoregressive Transformer to determine molecular size, atom types, coordinates, and chemical attributes.

ProtLingo, an efficient PLM framework that augments a pretrained single-sequence backbone with conditional local memory and sparse expert routing, achieves competitive performance with a 150M-scale backbone, including strong parameter efficiency on mutation-effect prediction and preserved long-range structural representations.

This study evaluated twelve regression models and conducted a large-scale virtual screening of over 11.5 million compounds, identifying 24 promising candidates of SERT inhibitor candidates, providing structurally diverse scaffolds and a computational prioritization framework for early-stage discovery and optimization of SERT inhibitor candidates that merit subsequent experimental validation.

OrbGNN is presented, an electronic structure graph architecture analogous to molecular graph and MLIP frameworks, where pair-orbital interactions constitute the graph representation, while orbital entanglement encodes the connectivity between them.

It is shown that neither high partial scores nor confident claims of completion reliably indicate that a scientific task has been fully delivered, highlighting the need to evaluate end-to-end workflow execution and the completeness of scientific deliverables together.

This work backmap an artificial neural network into a PNN simulation model using polymer networked nanoparticles (PNNPs), and tunes the plasticity of polymer linkers and the temperatures of nanoparticles to optimize the performance of the PNNP machines, which is analogous to tuning of the weights and bias of the corresponding ANNs.

A dynamical, target-docking translocase engine – the anthrax toxin protective antigen (PA) – is introduced as a label-free single-molecule peptide sensor to establish the requisite protein nanopore hardware for de novo proteomics.

TRACER (terpene rearrangement annotation via co-attentive enzyme-product representation), a multimodal framework mapping the latent associations between sequence-derived enzyme representations and product chemotypes, establishes a predictive paradigm for the rational discovery and mechanistic elucidation of complex terpene architectures.

Electrostatic embedding improved every accuracy and correlation metric for TYK2 but performed comparably to the classical and mechanical-embedding baselines for CDK2, thrombin, p38 and JNK1, and standard single-molecule energy and charge benchmarks were not good predictors of this target-dependent outcome.

This work presents an empirical analysis of UQ in deep learning models, focusing on genomics applications, and shows that Bayesian Neural Networks are better at capturing uncertainty caused by strong class imbalance and out-of-distribution data in genomics, despite their computational disadvantages.

A machine learning-guided quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) workflow was developed to prioritize fluconazole analogs and FDA-approved drugs with predicted antifungal activity against Candida, followed by a structure-based exploration of a cell wall target.

Self-Consistent UCG (SC-UCG), which uses the underlying UCG interactions directly to assign internal states without designing CVs in the CG ensemble, and enhances the RLE Hamiltonian with the Bethe approximation and AI-based inference to represent explicit correlations between UCG beads.

An integrated workflow for MLP/ΔMLP-assisted QM/MM simulations that achieves ab initio (ai) or density functional theory (DFT)-level accuracy in predicting enzyme reaction thermodynamics and incorporates an iterative model refinement strategy that systematically improves predictive performance through successive rounds of sampling, high-level labeling, and retraining.

AMPBench-MT is introduced, a provenance-preserving benchmark that standardizes canonical peptide records and organizes them into binary recognition, species-conditioned pMIC regression, and endpoint-specific potency and safety-facing readouts that shows that AMP evaluation should move beyond recognition leaderboards toward endpoint-aware evidence auditing.

PMRD separates mechanism-consistent factors from modality-specific information and constructs a consensus response domain across three modalities and combines complementary representations through reliability-aware multiview retrieval and supports PMRD as an effective framework for mechanism-aware multimodal drug representation learning.

BiteNetI is a structure-based deep learning model that uses 3D convolutional neural networks to simultaneously localize ion-binding centers and predict binding residues for 14 biologically relevant ions, supporting comprehensive and large-scale annotation of protein-ion interactions.

This review explores the current applications of ML technologies for predicting and managing the quality of livestock-derived foods and commonly used algorithms such as support vector machines, random forests, artificial neural networks, and deep learning architectures are reviewed in relation to their performance.

This work introduces point-group symmetry aware equivariant graph neural networks (PGEqNN) for materials science, with filter functions aligned with symmetry-aware indices for greater granularity in predictive tasks.

HEDGEHOG provides a reproducible benchmark for evaluating molecular generative models by measuring molecule survival through chemical filters and identifies stage-wise failure modes across generator classes and provides a practical basis for developing molecular generators better aligned with early drug discovery.

A machine learning-based framework for modeling thermal transport in bulk and nanocrystalline silicon by combining Gaussian approximation potential and multi-atomic cluster expansion models with lattice-dynamical calculations and molecular dynamics is developed.

A data-driven framework combining explainable machine learning (ML) with large-scale virtual library generation with large-scale virtual library generation is presented, establishing a practical route from experimental data to actionable catalyst designs.

DeepKinomeWeb is an integrated web-based platform that transforms competition-based high-throughput screening data into actionable insights for kinase inhibitor prioritization, and enables quantitative prediction of kinase–inhibitor binding affinities and panel-level visualization of selectivity landscapes, selectivity metric calculations, and integrated structural and physicochemical analyses.

A robust, standardized framework that integrates Raman spectroscopy with real‐time machine learning models and bioreactor control via OPC‐UA is developed, enabling seamless communication and effective control of mammalian cell culture CPPs.

This work demonstrates that publicly available KGs can be used for actionable, translational target discovery when coupled with clinical data and introduces Artemis, a practical and generalisable machine-learning framework for indication-aware target prioritisation that integrates public biomedical KGs with clinical evidence from the ChEMBL database.

The results establish Molexar as a practical unified foundation for computational chemistry and drug-design workflows and establish Molexar as a practical unified foundation for computational chemistry and drug-design workflows.

A machine learning framework was developed to predict Fe–S proteins using only sequence-derived features, including amino acid composition, cysteine-related metrics, and sequence length, which provides a foundation for large-scale, sequence-based discovery of Fe–S proteins and supports future investigations into their functional diversity across proteomes.

SMARTPocket-guided docking further improves near-native RNA-ligand pose recovery and computational efficiency compared with blind docking and establishes SMARTPocket as a generalizable framework for structure-based identification of ligandable RNA pockets and for accelerating discovery of RNA-targeted small molecules.

The results show that the degradation complexity and cross-cell heterogeneity affect the model performance, which highlights the importance of carefully designed evaluation protocols, statistical reliability analysis, and rigorous cross-cell validation to ensure reliable model benchmarking in lithium-ion batteries’ prognostics.
Chemical shift anisotropy KD (CSAKD), a novel method for determining absolute fragment affinities using NMR relaxation which seamlessly integrates into FBDD by NMR, is introduced.

This work proposes statistical principles for using synthetic data in scientific research with provable validity guarantees, and develops methods for valid inference under task exchangeability, together with extensions that provide guarantees even beyond exchangeability.

E-CloudBind improves drug-protein interaction (DPI) prediction by combining electron cloud representations with molecular graphs, enabling robust performance across low-resolution, predicted, and out-of-distribution structures for drug discovery.

A Fivefold Maximum Drug-Likeness strategy for prioritizing antibacterial candidates against Escherichia coli was developed and M2 was identified as a preliminary lead-like hit, although its mechanism, safety profile, and broader applicability require further validation.

An integrated computational drug-repurposing workflow combining machine learning-based potency prediction, structure-based docking, and molecular dynamics simulation to prioritize approved DrugBank compounds for mutant EGFR evaluation supports ML-guided docking and MD refinement as a practical strategy for prioritizing repurposing candidates for experimental EGFR validation.

The application of machine learning (ML) to learn the relationship between a set of biochemical parameters in single organelles of live cells and the best classifier, a shallow neural network, to classify the type of organelle using the biochemical parameters is explored.

Emp2lig is presented, a two-stage deep learning framework for automated ligand detection and atomic modeling directly from cryo-EM maps that provides a unified framework for ligand discovery and modeling across a broad range of resolutions.

A concise set of fairness definitions and metrics for DRL molecule generation offers practical guidance for reporting distribution parity and outcome parity and identifies open gaps relevant to trustworthy, cancer-relevant DRL generation.

This review reframes docking success from “obtaining a pose and a score” to earning confidence through transparent workflows and evaluation aligned with real use, with emphasis on how validation, generalization, and reproducibility requirements evolve in AI-assisted workflows.

inspired by medicinal chemists, who probe the pocket-ligand complex with controlled analog edits before choosing an optimization direction, PROBE is proposed, an optimization framework built around edit--response probing that achieves state-of-the-art performance and substantially mitigates the failure modes exposed by the diagnostics metrics.

SpinX is introduced, a GPU-native atomistic spin simulation framework built around a unified Hamiltonian interface and multiple user-selectable computational backends that supports deterministic and stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics, Monte Carlo sampling, static optimization, dynamical spectroscopy and string and geodesic nudged elastic band transition-path calculations on heterogeneous accelerator platforms.

AIMS-Fold is introduced, an inference-time guided-diffusion framework that actively steers the generative sampling trajectory using differentiable physical potentials derived from XL-MS spatial restraints and HDX-MS solvent accessibility profiles that achieves higher accuracy on challenging induced proximity targets than purely computational, unguided state-of-the-art models like Boltz-2.

Ensembits is introduced, the first tokenizer of protein conformational ensembles, which enables Ensembits to predict dynamics token from one single predicted structure, which alleviates dynamics data sparsity.

This work introduces EDMolGPT, a decoder-only autoregressive framework that generates molecules from low-resolution ED point clouds that mitigates structural bias and produces molecules with 3D conformations.

It is concluded that no single docking method dominates across targets and that rigorously validated, cost-effective combinations with supervised re-ranking currently offer the most practical value for virtual screening.

Q‐MRS is a DL framework based on a Convolutional vision Transformer that combines the strengths of a convolutional neural network (CNN) and a Transformer that produces fit quality and concentration estimates comparable with those of two established LCM methods, LCModel and Osprey.

The first HQC protein-ligand binding prediction using a mixed-basis set and an automated end-to-end workflow enabling practical HQC calculations of large protein systems is presented, presenting the first HQC matching coupled-cluster (CCSD) accuracy in fragment energies.

EVA-Flow is introduced, a unified framework for environment-aware molecular conformation generation that learns shared chemical structure and adapts it through environment-conditioned generative modeling and covers a broad range of solvation conformations.
By learning heterogeneous inter-graph interactions, the proposed method achieved state-of-the-art accuracy in predicting band gaps of 1,682 hybrid solar cell materials.

This work presents a hybrid quantum-classical workflow that combines molecular dynamics, density functional theory, and correlated wavefunction methods, tightly integrating CPUs, GPUs, and quantum processing units (QPUs) to enable simulations across multiple length and accuracy scales.

NOCE-Net, a deep nested sequence model that learns control-enabling representations directly from raw cyclic operational or telemetric data, and standardises heterogeneous aging datasets into semantically equivalent Full Equivalent Cycles defined by absolute charge throughput, enabling end-to-end learning across diverse operational regimes.

RNADaemon is presented, a framework that formulates RNA tertiary structure prediction as a Markov Decision Process and trains a Soft Actor-Critic agent to apply adaptive external force-field biases that steer all-atom molecular dynamics toward native-like conformations to minimize the eRMSD metric.

A virtual-atom formulation within the DPA3 framework, in which density query points are represented as virtual nodes and processed by the same parameterized encoder used for real atoms, which improves in-domain accuracy, makes local environment information more accessible under linear probing, and reduces zero-shot force errors on larger QM40 molecules.

PNBind is presented, a multimodal deep learning framework that leverages protein language models, evolutionary information, and three-dimensional structural features via a geometric vector perceptron (GVP) backbone with an invariant point attention (IPA) layer for nucleic acid-binding site prediction.

Solphin, a Python package for the generation, post-processing and analysis of photovoltaic calculations from periodic solid state Density Functional Theory, which includes the ability to calculate the photovoltaic Figure of Merit, detailed balance and spectroscopic limited maximum efficiency, alongside other analysis methods.

An automatic analysis pipeline that leverages denoising and unsupervised crystallographic analysis for 4D-STEM data is proposed that enables robust and automated analysis with significantly reduced analysis cost.

The combined approach provides a computational framework for prioritizing rare-earth-free soft-magnetic chemistries while distinguishing composition-level screening from candidate-specific physical validation.

CurvFM, a flow matching (FM) formulation whose training objective constrains the curvature at the generated structure, is introduced, a frozen Hessian prediction model that removes the need for quantum-chemical Hessians and keeps the residual cheap enough to impose at every training step.

This work introduces Mirror-Score, a calibrated, inference-only scoring framework for heterochiral D-peptide/L-protein complexes, and a public benchmark of 31 crystal complexes across four target families, including 18 with literature-verified affinities.

SPARC is introduced, a retrieval-guided test-time specialization framework that adapts a pretrained predictor using a spectral reference library without accessing test-query spectra to selectively preserve trustworthy predictions during continual specialization.

Results support the hypothesis that systematically curated assay metadata provides informative signal for affinity prediction, and develop a context-conditioned affinity model that injects an assay-context embedding into the Boltz-2 affinity module.

This study conducts extensive evaluations across a wide range of settings and demonstrates that ProFiT is a plug-and-play tokenizer adaptable to diverse downstream tasks and further reveals the significant potential of the flow matching tokenizer paradigm.

DualTopoDDI is proposed, a dual-topology-enhanced interpretable deep learning model for DDI prediction that offers a powerful, interpretable tool for understanding and predicting drug-drug interactions, providing critical insights for drug safety and design.

KRstereo is presented, a machine learning framework that predicts KR stereochemistry directly from sequence and improves reconstruction of polyketide structures from biosynthetic gene clusters and facilitates stereochemistry-aware genome mining and engineering of PKS assembly lines.

An explainable, assay-aware, and leakage-safe machine learning framework for predicting thrombin-inhibitory activity provides useful predictions within the represented chemical space and measurable generalization for unseen scaffolds.

Vulnerability-guided cascaded attention transformer (VCAT), which integrates Connectivity Map/Library of Integrated Network-based Cellular Signatures/LINCS-derived consensus transcriptional signatures with clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-supervised cellular representations through adaptive encoders and dual stream cascaded attention, outperformed conventional machine learning and published deep learning models.

Docking into open and intermediate TG2 conformations consistently ranked G11 as the most favorable candidate, with predicted binding near the catalytic core, with predicted binding near the catalytic core ranked G11 as the most favorable candidate.

Artificial intelligence should be viewed as an emerging decision-support tool that may strengthen precision medicine in PH while complementing clinical expertise across diagnosis, phenotyping, risk assessment, and therapeutic stratification pathways.

CysLENS (Cysteine Ligandability Evaluation through Neighborhood and Chemical Similarity), an integrative framework that prioritizes ligandable interactions by translating chemoproteomic screening data into interpretable cysteine–chemotype signatures, is presented.

This work introduces \textbf{MolEmb}, a lightweight framework that adapts MLLMs by aligning molecular profiles with textual descriptions in a shared embedding space using a bidirectional contrastive objective, and finds that context-aware molecular embedding is primarily a data property of the supervision.

TRACE is proposed, a transition-aware residual control framework that treats evaluated edits as the basic unit of feedback and improves over LLEMA, the state-of-the-art LLM-agent baseline, raising macro-average hit rate from 18.13\% to 25.96\%.

EvoBind-multimer is presented, a deep learning framework for the de novo design of molecular glues directly from protein sequences that generates small macrocyclic peptides that bridge user-defined protein pairs without requiring prior interface knowledge or existing ligands.

Pi-Ensemble (Predicting Interpolated Ensemble), a sequence-guided framework for generating protein conformational ensembles interpolating between two structural anchor states, provides an extensible framework for studying protein flexibility, guiding adaptive sampling, and accelerating mechanistic investigations of protein function.

MultiStructRNA enables seamless switching between prediction methods without requiring workflow changes and supports both in-notebook and exportable visualizations, and supports high-throughput analyses and simplifies comparison across methods while standardizing downstream feature extraction.

O3 proves most effective at low oracle budgets, while FK-steering and DPO demonstrate improved performance as the budget increases, and provides the first practical reference for oracle budget-aware guidance.

This study overcomes technical bottlenecks in real-time quality monitoring and process optimization for LV production, providing a feasible transition from "black box operations" to transparent and intelligent monitoring throughout the entire process and establishing a robust foundation for large-scale intelligent production of other gene therapy vectors.

Results consistently demonstrate that the coordinated integration of metaheuristic optimization, hybrid machine learning forecasting, and intelligent energy storage management provides a robust, reproducible, and scalable solution for improving the reliability, operational efficiency, economic viability, and sustainability of future smart distribution networks.

A multiscale workflow for coupling quantum computing algorithms for quantum chemical calculations with conventional high-performance computing (HPC) software and the resulting embedding framework combines a generic N-layer subtractive quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) scheme and selection of an active orbital space for the quantum algorithm region.

It is envisioned that foundation models for LC–HRMS data will benefit from the expansion of curated sample repositories and spectral libraries, developing privacy-preserving training strategies, enabling simultaneous modeling of multiple LC–HRMS data types, and improving model explainability.
